key_insight: A genome-guided, physics-informed screening framework can identify phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites by linking interpretable descriptors to stability and optoelectronic performance.
engineering_relevance: The approach narrows tens of thousands of candidate compositions to a few DFT-validated, all-inorganic semiconductor candidates for photovoltaics, sensors, and transparent electronics.
method: Trained ML surrogates on 1,221 DFT-calculated A2BB'X6 compounds using four descriptor families: packing, bonding, polarization, and electronic identity.
Applied a staged inverse-design filter to 13,088 charge-balanced, lead-free compositions to screen for thermodynamic stability and band-gap targets.
Validated top candidates with DFT, convex-hull analysis, and optical-property checks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong model performance, including ROC-AUC = 0.92 for stability classification and R2 = 0.93 for band-gap prediction on held-out data.
watch_item: The five shortlisted materials are DFT-validated, but experimental synthesis, defect tolerance, and long-term environmental stability still need confirmation.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
